name: Burton Electronics Manufacturing Services
old_description: Our team delivers precise, scalable electronics manufacturing powered by craftsmanship, accountability and pride in every assembly.
about:
Burton Electronics Manufacturing Services (Burton EMS) was founded in 1978 by Edward Leman and James Treiterer in New Berlin, Wisconsin. The family-owned company now maintains its headquarters in Hazelhurst, WI, and operates two manufacturing plants in Ironwood, MI. Operational control passed to Gary Burnett, Sr. in 1997, and the business remains family-led with Mark Leman as President & CFO and Gary Burnett Jr. as Vice President.

The contract manufacturer specializes in high-mix, low-to-medium volume electronics assembly, offering full product lifecycle support from design and engineering through production and end-market services. Capabilities include surface-mount and through-hole PCB assembly, box build, mechanical assembly, spray coating, and comprehensive testing such as burn-in and product validation. Facilities total over 26,500 square feet, including a 6,500 sq. ft. Hazelhurst plant and a 20,000 sq. ft. Ironwood facility expanded in 2006–2007, with a second Ironwood site added in 2021–2022 for high-level assembly and test. The company employs lean manufacturing, 5S, and Six Sigma methodologies, and uses 3D solder paste inspection and automated optical inspection for process control.

Burton serves OEMs in medical, industrial, motor control, specialized consumer, security, building controls, defense, and professional tool markets. Customers are described as industry leaders who demand high performance and reliability, and the company emphasizes long-term partnerships with program management and customer-focused teams.

The company states its differentiation lies in a "people-driven" culture that prioritizes direct communication, teamwork, proactive problem-solving, and integrity. It cites a warranty return rate below 0.5%, on-time delivery above 97%, and first-pass yield exceeding 99% as measurable outcomes of that culture. An intelligent DFM review using VAYO software with 1,500 design rules aims to eliminate defects early.
